Unless the process is stuck inside a C call (HiGHS) that doesn't release to the Python interpreter to process signals! Python signal handlers only run between bytecodes. If HiGHS is stuck in a long C computation, the handler is delayed until it returns. But 15s of HiGHS on a 5-variable LP?

Hmm, and SIGALRM would be delivered; the C code would be interrupted (EINTR) or the handler runs after the C call returns. If HiGHS loops forever, the handler never runs → the process loops forever consuming CPU → the tool's 180s CPU limit should kill it...
